Navigation Quick start Start here Get started API MCP Enterprise Use cases Quick start Start here Run your first search Where the papers come from Read the full paper Go deeper with Deep Review Save papers to your Library In ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or the API Understand your results Read a thread Check a claim Ask a paper Filter for recent studies Find popular papers Research terms dictionary Map the literature See how the field got here Spot the main findings Compare studies side by side Find where studies disagree Follow the trail Follow a paper's citations Grow a reading list from a paper Explore the citation graph Look up a researcher's work Organise and find gaps Build Collections for your project Find research gaps Add your own PDFs Beyond your first project Connect two fields Check a manuscript's citations Review a grant before you submit Catch up on a fast-moving field Key features Paper search Benchmarks Research Agent Deep Review Library Citation Graph Skills Extract data On this page Back to top How this guide works Where you can use Consensus Why researchers trust Consensus Plans Quick start Start here Copy page Copy page A short, video-first guide to Consensus for researchers at any level. Learn to search, read, and organise the literature on your topic, one lesson at a time. Copy page Copy page Consensus is an AI search engine for research. You ask a question, it searches over 400 million scholarly articles, including 350 million peer-reviewed research papers, and it writes an answer where every sentence links back to the paper it came from. It’s a search engine first. It finds the papers, then uses AI to read and summarize them. It doesn’t make things up from general knowledge, so you can always click through and check the source. How this guide works This guide is for researchers at any level, whether you’re starting your first project or you’ve been publishing for years. Each lesson is a short video plus a prompt to try on your own topic. Start at the top if you’re new to Consensus, or jump straight to the task you need. 1. Quick start Run a search, see where the papers come from, and save what you find. 2. Understand your results Read an answer, check its claims, and find the strongest papers. 3. Map the literature Find the main findings, the history, and where studies disagree. 4. Follow the trail Use citations to go from one good paper to many. 5. Organise and find gaps Keep your papers in one place and spot what’s missing. Key features Reference pages for search, Research Agent, Deep Review, Library, and more. All the videos are also in one YouTube playlist . New to research terms like “meta-analysis” or “preprint”? Keep Research terms in plain English open in another tab. Where you can use Consensus Web app Everything in this guide happens at consensus.app. It’s free to start. In ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or the API Connect Consensus to the AI assistant you already use in one click, or build on it with the API. Why researchers trust Consensus Search happens before AI. The AI only summarizes papers Consensus actually found. If nothing relevant turns up, it tells you. Every claim is checkable. Hover a citation to see the exact quote from the paper. See Check a claim against the paper . Retracted papers are flagged and never used in answers. Your data isn’t training data. Consensus doesn’t train models on your searches or uploads. It’s measured. In blinded evaluations judged by PhD researchers, Consensus finds more relevant papers than Google Scholar and than frontier models with web search. See Benchmarks . More relevant than Google Scholar 88.1% vs 81.8% precision on 500 real user queries, judged blind by PhD researchers. Beats GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8, 10x faster More relevant top-20 papers at a median of 8.7 seconds, versus 75 to 103 seconds. AI is a research assistant, not a replacement for reading. Use it to find and understand papers faster, then read the ones that matter. pages.title: Consensus: AI for Research
pages.text: Consensus: AI for Research Sign up Research starts here Sources Skills Deep Filter Build a comparison table Draft a report Get a Yes / No answer The new standard for academic research Search and analyze peer-reviewed literature. Consensus draws on 400M scholarly works, including licensed full text content from leading publishers. See all publisher partners Used daily at top research institutions Over 170 university libraries partner with Consensus to give students and faculty access. 10 million researchers, students, and clinicians use Consensus to supercharge literature reviews — without sacrificing academic rigor. About Us For Universities For Organizations Careers Contact Us Automate Literature Review with Deep Search Turn days of literature review into a few minutes. Consensus Deep Search builds a comprehensive search strategy, expanding key terms, identifying conflicting arguments, and exploring the citation graph. Compare randomized vs observational evidence on intermittent fasting Conflicting evidence on SSRIs and suicide risk in adolescents What are the competing theoretical explanations for the placebo effect in pain management? Try Medical mode Narrow your results to the highest-quality medical sources — about 50,000 clinical guidelines and 8M articles from the top 1,000 medical journals for quick, trusted clinical answers. First-line and second-line treatment for HFrEF with reduced ejection fraction SGLT2 inhibitors vs GLP-1 agonists for renal outcomes in type 2 diabetes Screening recommendations for colorectal cancer in high-risk patients Use filters with natural language Specify timeframes, populations, designs, and more directly in your prompt — and Consensus automatically applies the right filters for your search. Strongest clinical and population-level evidence on air pollution and cardiovascular disease Systematic reviews from the past 5 years on the impact of social media use on adolescent mental health How have findings on gut microbiome diversity changed over the last decade? See where the research agrees Ask a clear yes-or-no research question and the Consensus Meter instantly shows how much the evidence agrees or disagrees — giving you a fast, visual read on the state of the research. Do SGLT2 inhibitors reduce all-cause mortality in type 2 diabetes? Does air pollution exposure increase cardiovascular disease risk? Does intermittent fasting lead to meaningful long-term weight loss?

Navigation Introduction Get started with Consensus MCP Get started API MCP Enterprise Use cases Introduction Get started Plans and access What you can build with the Consensus MCP Tools Quick start: Search & Threads search create_thread get_thread add_to_thread find_threads get_full_text Connect your client Claude Desktop Claude Code ChatGPT Codex Cursor VS Code (GitHub Copilot) Windsurf Gemini Spark Perplexity Microsoft 365 Copilot Microsoft 365 Copilot Studio Other MCP clients On this page Back to top How Consensus compares Connect Your Client Using Consensus with ChatGPT Deep Research Verify Your Connection Plans and Access Tools Troubleshooting Security Supported Platforms FAQ Additional Resources Introduction Get started with Consensus MCP Copy page Copy page Search 400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers and all of PubMed, from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Microsoft 365 Copilot and other MCP clients. Copy page Copy page One hosted server covers every field of science, so you don’t need separate PubMed, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar servers. Your assistant gets ranked papers it can filter by study design, sample size and journal quality, and cites real studies in its answers. Connect your client below. You’ll be searching in under 2 minutes. What you can build with the Consensus MCP MCP is the fastest way to give an assistant or agent paper search. Owkin plugged Consensus MCP into its agentic AI scientist and went from curated PubMed abstracts to 25x the paper coverage in days. Browse the use cases. Server URL https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp Claude Add Consensus from the Claude connectors directory. ChatGPT Add Consensus from the ChatGPT app directory. Microsoft 365 Copilot Add Consensus for Copilot from the Microsoft Marketplace. Perplexity Add Consensus from the Perplexity Computer connectors store. How Consensus compares In blinded evaluations on real user queries, Consensus search returns more relevant papers than Google Scholar and than frontier models with web search. See Benchmarks . More relevant than Google Scholar 88.1% vs 81.8% precision on 500 real user queries, judged blind by PhD researchers. Beats GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8, 10x faster More relevant top-20 papers at a median of 8.7 seconds, versus 75 to 103 seconds. Connect Your Client Claude Desktop One-click: open Consensus in the Claude directory and click Connect . Or connect manually: 1 Open Settings Open claude.ai or the Claude desktop app and go to Settings . 2 Browse connectors Select Connectors , then Browse connectors . 3 Find Consensus Search for Consensus and click Connect . 4 Sign in Approve the sign-in with your Consensus account, or continue without one at reduced limits. 5 Start searching Ask a research question in any chat. Consensus appears in the tools menu. Claude Code claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp OAuth will open in your browser automatically on first use. You can also trigger it manually with the /mcp command inside Claude Code. ChatGPT One-click: open Consensus in the ChatGPT app directory and click Connect . Or connect manually: 1 Open ChatGPT Open chatgpt.com and sign in. 2 Find Consensus Open Apps from the sidebar, search for Consensus , and click Connect . 3 Sign in Sign in with your Consensus account when prompted. 4 Start searching Ask a research question, or call it by name: “Use Consensus to find RCTs on…” Search results display in an interactive widget showing top papers with citations and direct links. Consensus also works with ChatGPT Deep Research. See Using Consensus with ChatGPT Deep Research below. Codex codex mcp add consensus --url https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp codex mcp login consensus Or add to ~/.codex/config.toml : [ mcp_servers . consensus ] url = "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" Cursor One-click: Install in Cursor . Or add to ~/.cursor/mcp.json : { "mcpServers" : { "consensus" : { "command" : "npx" , "args" : [ "-y" , "mcp-remote@latest" , "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" ] } } } VS Code (GitHub Copilot) Add to your MCP configuration: { "servers" : { "consensus" : { "url" : "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" } } } Windsurf Add to your MCP configuration: { "mcpServers" : { "consensus" : { "serverUrl" : "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" } } } Gemini Spark Add Consensus as a custom app for Gemini Spark: 1 Open Connected Apps Go to gemini.google.com and sign in with a personal Google Account, then click Settings & help → Connected Apps . 2 Add a custom app Under Custom apps for Spark , click Add a custom app and paste the server URL: https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp 3 Approve the connection Click Next and follow the prompts to finish OAuth. If your client doesn’t support Dynamic Client Registration, expand Advanced features and enter your credentials. 4 Start searching Ask Gemini Spark a research question and it can call Consensus tools. Requires access to Gemini Spark, a personal Google Account, Keep Activity turned on, and is currently available in the US. Workspace and school accounts are not supported yet. Perplexity 1 Open the Consensus connector Go to Consensus in the Perplexity connectors store . 2 Add the connector Click + Add Connector . 3 Sign in with Consensus Complete the OAuth sign-in with your Consensus account. You need a Consensus account , which is free to create. 4 Confirm the connection Click Connect on the OAuth confirmation screen. 5 Open Computer Click Computer . 6 Ask a research question Say “Use Consensus to…” followed by a scientific question, for example: “Use Consensus to identify the pros and cons of GLP-1s.” Microsoft 365 Copilot In Microsoft 365 Copilot, Consensus is a connector your admin sets up for the tenant. Once it’s there, connect it yourself under Sources . 1 Open Copilot Chat settings In Microsoft 365 Copilot, select the gear icon at the bottom of the left sidebar, then Settings , then Sources . 2 Connect Consensus Find Consensus for Copilot and select Connect , then sign in with your Consensus account. 3 Ask a research question Type a research question like ‘What does the research say about creatine and cognitive function?’ and Copilot will call Consensus to find relevant papers. Don’t see Consensus under Sources? Your admin needs to add it first. Send them the Microsoft 365 Copilot admin guide . A Consensus account is required and free to create. Microsoft 365 Copilot Studio This allows you to add Consensus as a custom tool in Copilot studio so it can be used with agents or other automations you have have. This type of authentication will 1 Open custom tools Go to Copilot studio and find the ‘tools’ tab on the left hand side. 2 Create 'Create new tool' Click ‘new tool’ to add a custom tool 3 Click 'Model context protocol' You can also use the API to do this. But to use the MCP, click ‘model context protocol’. 4 Fill in the connector information Server name Consensus Server Description Consensus is the go-to MCP for academic research. Search 400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers, from PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and ArXiv — filter by study type (RCTs, meta-analyses, systematic reviews), journal quality, sample size, and more. Get structured results with citations, study takeaways, and direct links, or run pre-built workflows for literature reviews, grant research, and evidence synthesis. Server URL https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp Authentication OAuth 2.0 Type Dynamic Discovery 5 Save and use! Thats it! This custom tool can now be used and shared with other team members. Each team member will be able to connect to their own Consensus account when they use the tool. A Consensus account is required. It is free to create. API key (Bearer token) Use an API key for clients without OAuth, headless agents, and server-side automations. Send it in the Authorization header on every request to https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp : Authorization : Bearer YOUR_API_KEY Create a key from your profile icon under API & MCP Dashboard → Keys and clients → New key . The key gets its owner’s plan limits and draws from the same monthly pool as the API. See MCP plans and access . JSON config (Cursor, VS Code, and most clients that accept headers): { "mcpServers" : { "consensus" : { "url" : "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" , "headers" : { "Authorization" : "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $CONSENSUS_API_KEY" An invalid or revoked key fails the search with a tool error: “Your API key is invalid or expired.” Create a new key from the API & MCP Dashboard and update your client config. Keep the key server-side. Don’t paste it into prompts or commit it to a repo. Other MCP clients Any client that supports remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP) works. Point it at https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp . If your client supports OAuth, authentication is handled automatically. Pick your client for step-by-step setup. Watch: connect Consensus and run your first search Using Consensus with ChatGPT Deep Research Consensus also works with ChatGPT Deep Research. When Deep Research uses the Consensus app, it can search Consensus for relevant papers and retrieve full paper details for cited results. 1 Connect the Consensus app Connect the Consensus app in ChatGPT using the steps above. 2 Start a Deep Research request Start a Deep Research request in ChatGPT. 3 Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus for peer-reviewed research, for example: Use Consensus to research the evidence on exercise for depression. Prioritize systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and randomized controlled trials. Deep Research may run multiple Consensus searches, refine filters, retrieve paper details, and return a cited synthesis with direct links to papers on Consensus. Verify Your Connection Try one of these in your connected client. Each link opens the question pre-filled: Ask Try it ”What does the research say about creatine and cognitive function?” Claude · ChatGPT ”Find meta-analyses on mindfulness for anxiety published since 2020” Claude · ChatGPT ”Are there RCTs on intermittent fasting with more than 500 participants?” Claude · ChatGPT ”What is the strongest evidence for and against remote work productivity?” Claude · ChatGPT You should see results citing specific papers with titles, journals, years, citation counts, and direct links. Plans and Access Your Consensus plan, not your AI subscription, sets how many papers each search returns, your monthly calls, whether results include DOIs and full-text excerpts, and whether Threads can use deep mode. No account is needed to try it. Plans and access Limits for every plan, how calls are counted, additional usage, and API key access. Tools Consensus MCP exposes six tools. Your assistant picks the right one from your question. Tool What it does search Find ranked, peer-reviewed papers for a query in one call. get_full_text Read the complete text of open-access papers from search results or Threads, as Markdown. create_thread Start a Thread: hand a research question to the Consensus research agent. get_thread Poll a Thread and read the agent’s cited answer. add_to_thread Ask a follow-up in an existing Thread. find_threads List your Threads and find an earlier one. search works without an account. The thread tools need a signed-in Consensus account or an API key. get_full_text needs a paid plan. Quick start: Search & Threads When to use search, when to start a Thread, and how a Thread runs. Troubleshooting OAuth login is only supported for streamable HTTP servers (Codex) You added the server with -- --transport http instead of --url . Remove and re-add: codex mcp remove consensus codex mcp add consensus --url https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp codex mcp login consensus Authentication successful but server reconnection failed (Claude Code) Fully quit and restart Claude Code. Do not just use the reconnect option. Your credentials are saved and will work after restart. Tools stop working after a few hours (401 errors) Your OAuth token has expired. Re-authenticate: Claude Code: Type /mcp , select Consensus, choose Clear authentication, re-authenticate, then restart Claude Code Codex: Run codex mcp logout consensus then codex mcp login consensus Cursor: Disconnect and reconnect the server in Settings then Tools and MCP Claude Desktop: Disconnect and reconnect the connector in Settings then Connectors ChatGPT: Disconnect and reconnect the Consensus app from ChatGPT Apps Perplexity: Disconnect and reconnect Consensus in Computer then Connectors Server shows failed or no tools appear Verify the URL includes /mcp at the end Remove and re-add the server using the commands above Restart your client completely Consensus search has not been loaded yet (Claude Code) This is normal. Claude loads tool definitions on demand when many tools are present. Retry the query and it will work on the second attempt. ChatGPT Deep Research is not using Consensus Confirm the Consensus app is connected in ChatGPT Apps, then ask Deep Research to use Consensus explicitly. For example: Use Consensus to find peer-reviewed papers on this question and cite the strongest evidence. Deep Research decides when to call connected tools, so it may not call Consensus for questions that are not research-focused. No results found Try broadening your search query or removing filters. Use specific academic terminology rather than casual language. Monthly call limit reached Paid plans can continue making calls past the included monthly limit when the account has an active metered API subscription and additional usage is enabled; extra usage is billed at $0.05 per call, with each call covering up to 100 papers. Free plans must wait for the next monthly reset or upgrade. Rate limit exceeded (429 error) Rate limits are per user for authenticated MCP clients. A 429 that says you’re sending requests too quickly is a per-minute rate limit; wait a few moments and add backoff between requests. A 429 that mentions monthly call credits is a usage limit, not a rate limit. Security Endpoint: Only connect to the official URL: https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp API keys: Store securely using environment variables. Never share keys in prompts or public conversations. Rotate if compromised. Data handling: Search queries are sent to the Consensus API over HTTPS/TLS. Results contain publicly available academic paper metadata. No personal data is stored from MCP requests. Supported Platforms Platform Auth Status Claude Desktop OAuth Supported ChatGPT OAuth Supported ChatGPT Deep Research OAuth Supported Claude Code OAuth Supported Codex OAuth Supported Cursor OAuth Supported VS Code (GitHub Copilot) Config Supported Windsurf Config Supported Gemini Spark OAuth Supported Perplexity OAuth Supported Other MCP Clients Bearer token Supported FAQ Is there a PubMed MCP server with semantic search? Yes. Consensus covers all of PubMed plus the rest of science, ranked semantically rather than by keyword match alone. You can filter by study design, sample size, journal quartile and citation count. See Where the papers come from . What's the best MCP server for scientific literature in Claude? Consensus is in the Claude connectors directory and works in Claude on the web, the Claude desktop app and Claude Code . How do I add a scientific search connector to ChatGPT? Connect Consensus from the ChatGPT app directory . It also works with ChatGPT Deep Research . Can I use a research paper search MCP server in Cursor or VS Code? Yes. Install it in one click in Cursor , or add the server URL to your MCP configuration in VS Code (GitHub Copilot) . Which MCP server works for pharma and drug discovery? Consensus is SOC 2 Type II compliant, doesn’t use customer data to train AI models, and offers a zero-data-retention option on enterprise agreements. It runs behind AI gateways and in Microsoft 365 Copilot . Owkin uses it in its agentic AI scientist. See Security and data handling . Does it work for systematic reviews and meta-analyses? Yes. Filter by study design, including RCTs, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and run deep literature reviews with Threads. See the Threads quick start . Is this the same as Consensus (goconsensus.com)? No. This is Consensus, the AI academic search engine at consensus.app . It’s unrelated to the sales demo platform at goconsensus.com. Additional Resources Consensus Website Explore the Consensus research platform. API Documentation Structured JSON results for pipelines and integrations. MCP Specification Learn more about the Model Context Protocol. MCP server on GitHub View the source, report issues, and star the Consensus MCP server. Copy page Copy page If you already use ChatGPT, Claude, or Microsoft 365 Copilot, connect Consensus to it. Your assistant can then search over 400 million scholarly articles, including 350 million peer-reviewed research papers, apply academic filters, hand research questions to the Consensus research agent, and cite real research instead of answering from memory. Connect in one click Pick your assistant and add Consensus from its app directory. ChatGPT Add Consensus from the ChatGPT app directory. Claude Add Consensus from the Claude connectors directory. Microsoft 365 Copilot Add Consensus for Copilot from the Microsoft Marketplace. Sign in with your Consensus account the first time you connect. Your results depend on your Consensus plan, not your ChatGPT, Claude, or Copilot subscription. Connect another tool Using a different assistant or tool, such as Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Code? Connect it to the Consensus MCP server directly. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI assistants to use outside tools. The server is hosted, so there’s nothing to install: https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp Set up your client Step-by-step connection guides for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini Spark, Copilot Studio, and any other MCP client. What your assistant can do Search. The search tool returns ranked papers with title, authors, journal, publication year, citation count, study type, a key takeaway, and a link to the paper on Consensus. On paid plans it also returns query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers, so your assistant can quote the passage behind each claim. Your assistant can pass the same filters Research Agent uses: Year range, study type, and journal quartile (SJR) Human and controlled studies, minimum sample size, minimum citations Medical mode, open access only, exclude preprints Study duration and country Read whole papers. On paid plans, get_full_text reads the complete text of open-access papers from search results or Threads, so your assistant can work from a paper’s methods and results, not just its abstract. Threads. With a signed-in account, your assistant can also run Research Agent as a Thread. create_thread starts the agent on a research question, get_thread returns the cited answer when it’s ready, add_to_thread asks a follow-up, and find_threads finds earlier Threads. The agent can search your Library collections and save papers to them, and deep mode runs a longer literature review on paid plans. Quick start: Search & Threads When to use each, with a reference page for every tool. Supported clients Claude (web, desktop, and Claude Code), ChatGPT and ChatGPT Deep Research, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini Spark, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio, and any client that supports remote MCP servers. Claude ChatGPT Microsoft 365 Copilot Open Settings › Connectors , search for Consensus, and click + . Then switch it on from the + menu in any chat under Connectors . Open Apps , search for Consensus, and connect. It also works inside Deep research : open Sources and toggle Consensus on. In ChatGPT Deep research, Consensus appears under Sources. In Microsoft 365 Copilot, Consensus is a connector your admin adds for your organization. Once it’s there: Select the gear icon at the bottom of the left sidebar, then Settings › Sources . Find Consensus for Copilot , select Connect , and sign in with your Consensus account. Ask a research question, and Copilot calls Consensus to find relevant papers. Don’t see Consensus under Sources ? Send your admin the Microsoft 365 Copilot admin guide . You can use the MCP server without an account at reduced limits. Pre-built workflows Consensus publishes prompt templates (“skills”) for common research jobs you can run through MCP: Literature review helper — reconnaissance, PICO/SPIDER decomposition, systematic searching, and synthesis. Curriculum development — parse a syllabus into a reading list with discussion questions. Grant research — position your idea, map it to NIH institutes and mechanisms, and find funded overlap. See Skills , or browse the full gallery in Use cases . Use the API Building your own tool, agent, or workflow? The Consensus API gives you the same paper search over REST, and can run Research Agent as a Thread. Send a query, get back ranked peer-reviewed papers with metadata, and skip running each search by hand. It’s self-serve and open to everyone. GET https://api.consensus.app/v1/search The top 20 most relevant papers per query by default; raise page_size for more, up to your plan’s maximum Metadata on every paper: title, authors, journal, year, DOI, citation count, and a link On paid plans: study design, journal rank, key takeaways, and query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers The same filters as the web app: publication date, study type, sample size, citations, journal quality, field, country, and open access To get a key, click your profile icon in Consensus, choose API & MCP Dashboard , open Keys and Clients , and click New key . Get started with the API Authentication, your first request, and the full parameter reference. Run Research Agent from code Start a Thread, wait for the cited answer, and ask follow-ups. Plans and limits API and MCP calls share one monthly pool. Plan Max papers per call Included calls per month Rate limit Extra fields No account 3 No monthly limit 5 per second, shared — Free 10 30 1 per second — Pro 300 500 3 per second Study type, takeaway, DOI Deep 750 2,000 3 per second Study type, takeaway, DOI Teams 300 500 3 per second Study type, takeaway, DOI Enterprise 1,000 Custom Custom Study type, takeaway, DOI A call covers up to 100 papers: 1–100 papers is 1 call, 101–200 is 2, and so on. Requests default to 20 papers. Paid plans can enable additional usage at $0.05 per call, up to 1,000 calls per month (10,000 on Deep). It’s off by default. Usage resets on the 1st of each month. See MCP plans and access for the full breakdown. Track usage, connected clients, and billing from your profile icon under API & MCP Dashboard . Connected MCP clients appear under Keys and clients, alongside your API keys. Clients without OAuth can pass any Consensus API key as a Bearer token. The key gets its owner’s plan limits. See MCP plans and access . For custom Enterprise limits, contact [email protected] . Security Only connect to the official URL above. Queries travel over HTTPS, results contain publicly available paper metadata, and no personal data is stored from MCP requests. Related Get started with MCP Connect your client in under 2 minutes. Useful before a meeting, a hire, or a citation. Copy page Copy page Sometimes you need to understand one person’s footprint: what they’ve published, and what influence it’s had. Instead of scouring ResearchGate or Google Scholar, ask Consensus. The example uses a PhD candidate with a handful of papers, not a famous name, to show it works for early-career researchers too. You’ll learn how to: Run an author-scoped search filtered by topic Rank a researcher’s papers by citation impact Visualize the citation graph and regenerate it with several seeds Step 1: Find the author’s papers on a topic Find papers by Alysha D'Souza on muscle development in female athletes and identify the most influential paper in that set. Research Agent resolves the correct author, finds their papers, narrows a broad set of ~12,000 results to the ones where they’re a primary author or co-author on the topic, and identifies the most influential one. In the example, that’s an umbrella review with 102 citations. Click through to the DOI to confirm authorship. Step 2: Trace the paper’s impact Show me later work that was built on that paper and summarize its impact. Consensus walks the citation graph forward, finds ~55 eligible citing papers, shortlists 20, and summarizes how the field responded. In the example, the review exposed methodological flaws, and later studies moved from calendar-based to hormone-informed cycle tracking. Step 3: Triangulate with the citation graph Scroll up to the original thread, click the paper, and click Graph . A new tab opens with the 15 papers most related to it, forward and backward. Open the sidebar, add two or three more papers as seeds, and click Regenerate graph . The graph now shows papers related to all of the seeds together, which is a fast way to find work on a narrow niche. Reading and refining the graph Each seed gets a color; papers one hop away take that color. Gray nodes bridge clusters. Horizontal axis is time; node size is citation count; opacity shows how connected a paper is. Arrows point from a paper to the paper it cites. Hover a node to highlight its connections. + Seed promotes a result to a seed; the minus button excludes it; Density switches between 20, 40, and 60 papers. Click Chat at the bottom to ask questions with all seeds and results attached. Graphs aren’t saved yet (beta), so promote seeds and save the papers you care about to your Library before closing the tab.
